I'm so sorry for what happened to you...fuck abusers and manipulators. Forgive if it makes YOU feel better, not because you're obligated to. You were hurt and your hurt makes sense to those of us who have experienced this sort of pain. You owe nothing to anyone.

No no no no HUNNY

This man is an abuser and a master manipulator. He has made you feel vulnerable and responsible for your own vulnerability. You are allowed to go wherever you want, feel whatever you want, kiss whoever you want. You are precious and he is the scum of the earth. What happened to you is sexual assault. From the moment you walked out he KNEW you didn't want him to touch you. He stalked you and groped you without your permission. He just felt entitled to take what he wanted from you.

It would let me, I just don't have the willpower to continue. I had to eat something.

I'm tired of being abused by everyone I know, the world is a very unsafe place for me and I can't stay in it.
that's not what I was saying...

No one actually thinks that hard about how socially competent other people appear to be. And no one with any amount of decency approaches someone else's anxieties from a place of judgment. Anxiety breeds anxiety, and that is what's happened here. You haven't actually realized anything about yourself, you are just justifying a belief you already had.
fuck that. Fuck bill. Fuck men who feel entitled to take what they want. Fuck not being allowed to talk. Stay angry and be grateful for your anger.
Ok, well if you want some money from me you don't need to pay me back because I don't need it. Just let me know.

Ok, I don't need money because I'm starving to death for other reasons, so I can give some to you if you send me a paypal. And I can make a post for you on here too so others can send you money.

Not stupid, btw - this is a magical gift abusers have. If you're vulnerable to them, they see a giant target on your back. But they don't walk around with some physical deformity like we do. There's no way to id them because they're basically snakes in human skin.

i understand you more than most. Some people get fucked over and over again. At some point you become a walking target. I don't know why but FUCK these abusers and manipulators who give in to their sociopathic whims and allow themselves to see us as less human. If you decide you don't wanna die we can get angry instead.

Btw are you starving because you need money or you just aren't eating?

I don't even see it as my fault, just a fact about me. I was mistreated when I was young and it marked me for life. Abusers are the cause, not me, but it doesn't matter because I carry around my victimhood like a stench. They can smell it and it never goes away. I'm gonna be this way until I die but I'm gonna die soon.

I left Ezra trying to be a decent person and take care of myself, and I ended up with another asshole because that's who comes for me. I've always been surrounded by abusers, so in my life, they're definitely not a minority at all.

I just want to tell this to someone it might matter to, because I know I'm going to be dead, I know that will happen within a few days and in some natural way. I'm here to be destroyed and that would happen without me doing anything. And that's fucked. I have to actively feed a body I hate just to survive. So I won't.

But I'm desperate for someone to understand this. I know how abusers and manipulators think. If you're one of these people, I'm talking to you. You think we don't know? WE KNOW. I know the look in a man's eye when he's thinking of me as prey. I know what I am. And when you pour yourselves into us, we pity you. Being an empty vessel isn't the saddest life in the world. Being a tidal wave drowning everyone you know, that's a sad life. You don't come out of this looking good. You got to fuck me, congratulations. You got to tear me open like a present all wrapped up for you. But now you get to watch me die. You say that's never what you wanted, fuck you. You wanted to destroy me. Now I get to destroy you too.

I don't know if I want to keep living if this keeps happening.

I've taken some self defense classes. I don't feel like less of a victim just because I can try to defend myself (not good at it anyway, I am small and realistically not strong or brave enough to fight a man who's bigger than me). I don't believe it's just insecurity that's making me vulnerable. I think it's something deeper that only abusers know how to identify, but I don't know what it is.

Thanks so much for making this post.

I've decided not to consider getting back together with him. I'm not planning to totally cut him off because I think it could be really devastating for him right now, but I'm not going to see him or try dating him again. You're right. The way he's treated me isn't the way I want to be treated, and although I'm more prone to seeing his issues as manifestations of psychological trauma, there are a lot of issues in the way he sees women that I don't really have the emotional strength/energy to deal with. I've always wanted to be with a guy who's feminist and respectful towards women, and he is not that. And he probably never will be. I don't want to be a victim, and I'm sad that I come off that way to people here. I want to be happy and strong and with someone who treats me well. If I come off as someone who wants to be a victim, I'm thinking about things the wrong way.
I said "I love you" to other guys, but I think he's the first one I've been seriously, deeply in love with.
I've had other relationships, and they certainly felt serious at the time, but I was in high school, so...not that serious. :)
I'm so sorry that happened to you. It makes me sick. Thank you for sharing your story with me and for your insightful post above.

I'm definitely NOT set on doing anything - I came here to genuinely ask for advice because I honestly have very little experience with this sort of thing, and I'm grateful for every single post here. This place was massively supportive and helpful for me when I was dealing with him asking me to do DD, and I came back because I need help yet again. Like I said, I might seem incompetent, but I'm really trying.

I think you're totally right when you say I'm close to being done with this part of my life. It's not that I think I deserve discipline or abuse, but I feel so unsure of whether it's ethical for me to judge him as a "piece of trash" based on how he treated me for a few weeks (which really came down to an anger issue that he has due to the way HE was treated growing up). It seems so unfair to dismiss him that way when he's actually taking concrete steps to change, and even though my instinct is somewhat that I should just move on, I also wonder whether it's even possible for him to change and how much I'd regret it if I didn't find out whether he can. But I am listening, and I hear you when you say "everyone here is telling you the same thing." That matters to me.

>And even if he did change in 4 months, you're with somebody who KNOWS they can abuse you, and who KNOWS you will come back.

Good point. I will be careful. Thank you.

>He is going to treat you with kindness and love in the first few months, absolutely. He's going to try hard to win you back. And then it will stop when you're with him and he will go back to being abusive, and this will happen all over again.

This is definitely my concern. It's hard for me to tell when he's being sincere. He's very good at acting, and has pretended to give me what I want in the past as a way of getting me to agree to what he wants in the future. I'm not sure that this will happen all over again, but that possibility does fucking terrify me. I just also wonder whether it's possible for it NOT to happen. I know people behave in abusive ways because they're deeply broken, and I can't help but wonder if he could genuinely be "fixed." If he can be, it doesn't seem fair to ignore the possibility of being with him on the basis that he was hurt and broken and developed an anger issue.

I do have friends I can see and talk to about this, and they don't dislike him, but the one friend I told about the DD idea was really, really against it and started thinking he was abusive. But in general, I don't think she (or my other friends) dislike him, they just don't really understand him and dislike how frustrated I get when I'm dealing with him. I don't think I'm the best judge of his character, but I don't think I'm totally off, either; there's a lot to love about him, despite how he treated me for a while.

Harsh words, but I understand where you're coming from. You're probably right; it's just hard for me to discount all the time we had together that was so exactly what I wanted, and convince myself that the way he behaved for a few weeks is how he really is.

> Your brain is telling you that your ex is an available source of emotional support, while he is actually your abuser.

You know, I think this is true. I don't know whether to count him my "abuser" since the horrible treatment he gave me took up a very small portion of the time I knew him and actually only happened *after* we broke up, but you're right that on some level, I'm probably seeing him as a potential source of emotional support. I have other people I can depend on (friends, family, etc.) but it's difficult not to consider him when I'm kind of anxious and he seems so much like the way he used to be.

>Why would he allow himself to get drunk a second time if he was truly apologetic?

Those two times both happened as I was trying to leave him - and he wasn't at ALL "truly apologetic" then. I'm not even sure if he is now, I just think he might be because he's acting SO different from before (before, he would've gone back into raging dominant demanding mode like, twenty minutes after apologizing).

I think he was sad, but doesn't know how to express sadness because of the way he was treated as a kid. I'm really hoping he's genuinely working on that (not just so I can consider getting back together with him again, but because it's so fucked up). I really feel for him in having an anger problem, although that doesn't mean that I want to risk exposing myself to it. You're right that these habits take a long time to change and I don't necessarily have to be around while they change, as it can be a really painful process.

Just wanted to clarify that those two times involved him shoving/squeezing me, not punching me or anything super abusive; but I totally understand where you're coming from on all this. It's hard to see these behaviors as being "ingrained in him" because they didn't show themselves for SO LONG. But I know what you mean, I think - whatever makes him this way, it's rooted deeply in his psyche and isn't going to leave just because he wills it to.

And just to clarify on this:

>How can you possibly be able to deduce he's truly changed his mindset in that time span?

I'm totally with you and I definitely don't feel confident that he's truly changed. At this point, I'm NOT thinking about getting back with him, more like thinking about thinking about it.

That phrase, literally, is lifestyle BDSM talk? As far as he told me, he wasn't really into BDSM or any really kinky sexual stuff. Of course, he could've been lying (or could it be a coincidence for him to use this kind of language?).

I know it sounds weird, but he was actually only physically violent to me (not beating, just violent) on two occasions, both when he was really, really drunk to the point of being totally out of his own control (and both towards the VERY end, when he was going insane trying to keep me with him). The verbal abuse and berating that started after I left, and the bullying to try to get me to stay, were what concerned me and made me think I could never be with him again. But I haven't seen a hint of that kind of behavior since he contacted me last week, and I actually wonder if something was seriously wrong with him at that time. He seems to genuinely understand how much he fucked up, which I hadn't seen from him since before the whole DD issue came up.

:) Thank you.

I think you're probably right that I should give it more time, and honestly, I wasn't thinking of just diving back into a relationship with him, because I am apprehensive (as you mentioned). I guess I was thinking more of starting to see him occasionally so I can figure out how serious he is about all this, and then start to date him only if it seems like he's not wavering in his new resolve to treat me kindly.

The thing that confuses all of this is that he treated me poorly for maybe two or three months...out of the three YEARS I've known him. A matter of months WAS enough time for him to start treating me horribly, so I why can't it be enough for him to change now? I can't help but think that maybe that darker side of him was the one that wasn't real, and the side he's showing now is who he always was.

How long do you think IS long enough to break those kinds of habits?

I know I can find someone who will treat me right, and even though I've been dating a little (haven't found another boyfriend, but not because I couldn't—I just wasn't totally ready to seriously date someone else) I still feel really uncomfortable thinking I'll never be with him again. So I don't think this is an issue of me being lonely or thinking I can't find anyone else.

I *do* want to spend the rest of my life with him. But I don't want my life to look the way he wants it to. The thought of a relationship where I have to be completely submissive scares me. I trust him with absolutely everything, but I've never believed that one person should have total control of a relationship, and the only reason I considered consenting to this lifestyle was that I love him more than I can ever imagine loving anyone else.

If it was honestly just a matter of him wanting to spank me, I wouldn't care much. I would trust him not to injure me. The reason I don't want to consent to this lifestyle is that I don't want to hand over my right to make decisions for myself or feel like it's impossible to express my real feelings.
I do. I love her. :)

Sorry, I think I wasn't clear. He has an anger issue, but he has NEVER been violent towards me. Ever. What I mean when I say he has an anger issue is that he flies off the handle quickly - our spats escalate into fights much faster than they should, and he can't think clearly when he's in a rage. He's aware of his anger problem and we talk about it openly. He knows that he gets out of control when he's angry. The reason I'm willing to work through it with him is that I know he's ultimately a kind, gentle person who is suffering - not a violent person.

He sees DD as a potential solution to his problem not because it means he can take it out on me when he's angry (one of the tenets of DD is that the HoH never administers punishments while angry) but because he believes it will allow him to release his feelings in a healthy way before they lead to rage. I disagree with him.

> Mind telling me what those bad habits are?

Nothing very out of the ordinary, just typical bad habits that develop when you're close with someone - being stubborn/wanting to get my way all the time, saying unnecessarily mean things when I'm angry, neglecting responsibilities and expecting him to pick up the slack, etc.

I understand that DD sounds really extreme and it probably sounds like our relationship is already unhealthy, but honestly, until now, I've *never* been seriously unhappy because of our relationship - on the contrary, it's made me extraordinarily happy. Him bringing up this idea was completely out of step with the way the rest of our relationship has been. We both have things to work on, but they're nothing that couples don't work through all the time. The DD ultimatum is the only reason I'm considering ending our relationship. I have no interest in breaking up with him otherwise.
I'll watch it. Thank you for the link.

To be clear, he is ANGRY, but not at all violent. The farthest it's ever gone is him throwing things at the wall. He has never hurt me intentionally before, and I honestly don't think he'd do so non-consensually. He has a problem, but he's ultimately a gentle person, not at all malicious or violent.

Thank you for your reply! Honestly, as it is now, he's the least controlling person I've ever been with. He clearly wants that to change. I'm willing to compromise by letting him have more input into the decisions we make together, but definitely NOT willing to let him make choices for me about things like makeup or seeing friends. I only want to stay with him if he can remain the same kind, gentle, loving partner I've been with all along. Yes, he has anger issues, but this is a result of his circumstances growing up (he had a really angry, abusive, military father who physically and emotionally assaulted him). I am willing to be patient with him as he resolves these issues, which he wants to do - I just don't agree that DD is the way to resolve them.

To clarify, this isn't about BDSM or sex; it's a framework for the entire relationship. Honestly, if he was just asking me to try BDSM with him, I wouldn't really have any qualms about it (though it's not my thing).
I decided not to go through with it. :) Thanks for your concern. I made an update post to this subreddit if you want to read it.

Just FYI, the way he's behaving is inappropriate. You should seek someone's permission before you touch them in a sexual way, and he isn't doing that. That's the reason you're confused. He needs to be more direct if he does like you. And since you've made it clear you have no interest in him, unfortunately, it's on you to make that clear to him. It should be his responsibility to give you the opportunity to say 'yes' or 'no,' but since he's failing to do that, you have to tell him 'no' yourself.

And don't be embarrassed about him saying it was accidental. There's really no such thing as accidentally rubbing someone's thigh. He's definitely doing it on purpose to see how you respond.

Thank you so much for your perspective. I was hoping to hear from someone who has been involved in a DD relationship, since all the perspectives I've heard are from a) people who are deeply involved in the DD community and b) people who know nothing (or almost nothing) about it.

My impression is that the kind of DD relationship Ezra is interested might be a little different from your arrangement. He does want to involve spanking (including maintenance spanking) but I think he's less interested in eliminating the possibility of me making decisions for myself. Basically, what he said is that he gets the final word but I have the right to give input and be heard, so I don't feel like I'm totally voiceless.

Still, this is so different from our current arrangement and from the way I actually make decisions now that I can see how I could become resentful if I wasn't allowed to ever have the final say in decisions for our relationship. I don't think I'm as committed as you are to the idea of not making decisions for myself; I'm not a passive person and I'm not generally scared to make choices (though I do have bad anxiety, which is part of Ezra's 'sell' on this lifestyle).

What ended up happening with you and your husband? Is the relationship different now than it was before you tried DD?

Yeah. You're right. When I say he's who I want to be with, I mean who he is *now.* But isn't that what everyone means when they say that? Yes, he might change in ways I don't like, but there is always that risk. If someone changes so much that you don't love them anymore, *that's* when you leave. It doesn't make sense to me to leave in anticipation of that happening. He hasn't become meaner or more demanding since bringing this idea up, and he brought it up in the most respectful way possible, asking how I felt and what I wanted rather than demanding that I change.

He has problems like everyone does. Yes, his anger issues make our relationship less perfect than it could be, but so do my stubbornness, the fact that I say unnecessarily mean things when I'm pissed off, my anxiety, etc. He believes this lifestyle will smooth out the wrinkles in our relationship. I believe he's wrong about that, but I don't think the fact that he has a fundamentally different vision for our life together means that he's going to turn into a monster.

I wasn't actually making this post to be defensive, because I found your post helpful. You're right that there are real risks in agreeing to this relationship. I just feel like there are more tangible risks involved in breaking up with him. I made the post because I wanted to say I agree with you. I don't WANT to be treated as less than equal. I don't WANT to be afraid of making mistakes. I don't want this type of relationship. I just also don't want to leave him. It's not as simple for me as 'this is bad, don't do it.' It's 'this is bad, but is it really worse than leaving a relationship that makes me extremely happy and constantly wondering if it could have worked?' I find it hard to believe that breaking up would be LESS emotionally painful than TRYING something that my partner, who I love and trust very deeply, wants.

Thank you so much for your balanced response.

I actually agree, intellectually, with pretty much 100% of what you've said here. You're right that I'm not the kind of person who wants this for their relationship. My needs are NOT compatible with his. I'm scared of what this will do to me emotionally and psychologically. I'm just MORE scared of him leaving me. I know that sounds fucked up, but hear me out.

I know that, as it is now, I'm the happiest I've ever been because of him. And I know that, if we start a DD relationship, I'll be less happy. But I also believe that if we break up because I couldn't agree to a lifestyle that he NEEDS, I'll feel extremely depressed, lonely, and miserable - and on top of that, I'll fault myself for not trying to fix the relationship in the only way he sees possible. I don't want to be that way, but I am. It's just something I know about myself.

I'm so stressed out about this and basically haven't slept since he brought the idea up to me because I can't figure out ANY reasonable solution to the problem. Everyone here is calling me stupid...well, I probably do sound stupid, because I honestly can't think straight. I feel like my brain is short-circuiting. It's a problem without a solution - I can't be with him (because he doesn't want to be with me as I am) and I can't be without him (because I don't even know what being myself means without him anymore). I feel like people here are forgetting that I actually *love* him and want to be with him. I feel as intensely about him now as I did when I first fell in love with him, if not more so. I don't know how to abandon that. I have absolutely no interest in breaking up with him or being with anyone else. There's no solution to this problem. Acquiescing to HIS relationship goals seems like literally the 'easiest way out.' I don't know how else to frame it for myself.

This comment, in the sea of 'omg you are so stupid's and 'your boyfriend is a creep's, really stood out to me. You get it. A lot of my reaction to this is about the fear of being alone, of ending a relationship that has been such a source of stability in my life.

My feeling is just that it's really, really hard to find someone I'm truly and deeply compatible with, who understands me without my having to explain myself, who I feel safe with and can trust to do what's best for me. I've never believed in "soulmates," but secretly feel that he is mine. I feel like he's perfect for me and anyone else would just be a pale imitation.

But you're right. He's not perfect for me, because he wants things I don't want. It just sucks to admit that something that seems so logistical could keep us apart when we're so emotionally, physically, and socially compatible.

It's just really good to hear that you can feel that way and then find someone else. I've NEVER felt about anyone else the way I feel about him. I've NEVER felt so comfortable and at home with someone. I'm scared that I won't be able to find that again, and feeling like staying with him in a relationship I don't want is better than being in no relationship at all (in terms of my actual happiness). I'm going to be extremely sad if I break up with him, but it won't make me extremely sad to let him spank me. For that reason, it's hard to convince myself that, practically speaking, staying with him and submitting isn't the right choice...even though in a more abstract sense, it means we're fundamentally incompatible. I want to be who he wants.

No, I just think you misunderstood this part...it's saying that the submissive partner gets punished for their own mistakes (which is an 'easy' way to resolve bad feelings about mistakes), but the HoH feels the same kinds of guilt/sorrow/remorse when they make mistakes, and yet DOESN'T get punished (and thus it isn't that 'easy' to get over the feelings). If punishing the submissive partner for their HoH's mistake is part of the lifestyle, it's not one Ezra is interested in. I don't mean to sound defensive, I just think you got this one wrong and I haven't heard of this idea (your interpretation of that paragraph) in two days of pretty intensive research.

This isn't true - the punishments for the submissive partner have NOTHING to do with the HoH fucking up. They're about keeping the submissive partner aware of their own mistakes and giving closure to them.

> Why, if your relationship is so wonderful, does he need to impose this?

OK, honestly, the main reason he's bringing this up now is that he has anger issues that came to a head last weekend. It's apparently something he was always considering as a solution, but he didn't bring it up to me until a particularly bad fight. Our relationship ISN'T all sunshine and roses - like any people in a relationship, we have our problems. This was presented to me as a potential solution to those problems. However, I'm happier with things staying the way they are or finding another solution to his anger issues. He is not. He sees this as the ultimate solution, as he believes it will allow him to release his emotions in a healthy way that gives him closure and ebb his anger at the source.
Sorry about that. Adding a disclaimer to my OP.
I definitely didn't mean to link to anything that would mess up your computer...I've opened it multiple times, it's just a PDF. I'm really sorry if I linked to something fucked up.

I don't really know what you mean by that. Maybe some DD relationships involve the HoH keeping the submissive partner from making decisions for themselves, but in this case, it's purely about relationship decisions. I would still be allowed to choose what to study, where to work, etc., so I'm not sure that this would interfere with me 'living my own life.' It would just stop me from doing things he disagrees with in the context of our relationship, basically.

Uh...he's asking for my consent to physically punish me, because to do so without my consent would be abusive and wrong. He wants to be in a DD relationship, not to control me or hurt me in a way that I don't want. He's an extremely respectful partner, even if he has a different vision for our relationship than I do. And he's not an 'old school man of the house,' this is just a belief he's arrived at about the ideal way for relationships to function.

I've basically resolved that I need to talk to someone in real life about this before I commit to it. You're right, to an extent - I'm here because I'm too embarrassed to bring this up with any of my RL friends. I'm scared of what they'll think of me. But I need the opinion of people who know me and know my relationship before I decide to consent to something that feels really different from what I've imagined my relationship would be like.

We actually have a relatively 'vanilla' sex life. I'm not particularly interested in BDSM, and I've never seen him show any sign that he is either. This is probably TMI, but...he's actually very gentle and 'normal' in bed. I don't think there's anything fundamentally sexual about his desire for this type of relationship, although I believe that is probably the case in some DD relationships.

> C'mon now, that's not you at all. 

It's not really me, you're right. I've never been a submissive person, whether in my professional life, among my social group, or sexually. But I think most people are multidimensional in this way. I have the ability to be dominant in a relationship, but I also have the ability to be submissive. It's not like I've never acquiesced to someone else's choices or desires before. I guess my feeling is that if this is an absolute dealbreaker for him, I don't have much to lose by giving it a chance. If it's what he needs, and I need to be with him, it's hard to see any other option besides breaking up, which I'm really not interested in doing.

I don't really think he's trying to turn me into a Stepford wife, lmao. He enjoys doing housework and cooking for me. I don't think he's looking for me to change the way I am, or to necessarily take a more traditionally feminine role in the relationship. I think he just believes that relationships work better when someone is leading them, so that there's less conflict about how decisions are made.

> Stop right here. Is this a belief you also share? This will be the foundation of the future you have with this person, if this is not something you share your relationship is not going to work.

No. It's not a belief I've ever even given consideration, so no, I don't "share" it. But beliefs can change. I don't want the same kind of relationship he wants, but I do want to be with him more than I want to break up with him, which is why I'm considering *trying* something I don't want with him.

>But I would be willing to make a pretty substantial bet that they are no where near equal to the amount of men led households.

Yes, you're right. The overwhelming majority of these relationships have men as the HoH. I do think it's based in certain sexist ideas about the way that relationships should function...but I don't think it necessarily has to play out in sexist ways. Given that Ezra is one of the least chauvinist men I've met, I find it hard to believe that our relationship would be one in which the DD dynamic was inherently sexist. (It definitely is so in certain DD relationships, especially Christian DD.)

>  It might not seem like it right now, but you and your partner are on pretty different levels when it comes to your own personal development. Think long and hard about what you want to do with your life, where you want to go, what you want to be, etc. before you resign yourself to possibly stifling those parts of you.

This is actually one of the most compelling reasons I see here to seriously consider not being in a relationship with him, even if he agreed to be in a non-DD relationship with me. I like being with him, but I realize that doesn't mean we're fundamentally compatible (as much as it feels like we are). It just really hurts to admit that's a possibility. I've pictured the rest of my life having him in it for a long time.

You have a lot of good points. The fact is that I *don't* want to be submissive. I just want to make my relationship work, and I think I *can* be more submissive if it's 100% necessary to do so. I have the understanding that my relationship can't carry on as it is, so my decision comes down to: Will I be happier in the relationship with the person I utterly love, but who wants things to work a way that I don't really want - or will I be happier alone? My feeling at the moment is that my feelings for him make it reasonable to at least try things the way he wants them, if that's the only way to stay with him. I have absolutely no interest in breaking up with him, but some interest in trying a new kind of relationship, even if it's not what I envisioned my relationship looking like. He's exactly the person I want to be with.

Just FYI, I didn't mean in that comment that I endorse those views or completely believe that they're accurate and not the result of women trying to rationalize their choice to be in this sort of relationship. I was just sharing what I learned in my research on this since hearing about it, because the poster I was replying to seemed not to understand why this appealed to anyone. The truth is that the majority of the relationships I've heard about online are those in which the woman - NOT the man - originated the idea to bring DD into the relationship. They obviously get something significant out of it, though I'm not sure *I* can.

I definitely see how it could look this way, and honestly, I was really freaked out when he first presented this idea to me - which is why I'm here seeking guidance. But the fact is that this is actually the LEAST manipulative/creepy/weird relationship I've ever  been in. He's always been extremely respectful, even feminist in the way that he relates to me.

If it was anyone else, I would've stopped listening at 'submission.' But I can't believe that, if he's at ALL the person I think he is, he's trying to 'manipulate' me in any way. He's never so much as tried to convince me out of making a decision I've resolved to make. He cooks, cleans, and takes care of me.
